messages:
maria: Heads-up — after yesterday's long-context replay run I'm seeing steady RAM creep on kv-cache hosts, specifically tied to lots of 1–3 token microblocks not being reclaimed.

maria: repro steps: stress-run with longpriorities, then switch kernel-selector to 'latency-favor' and run 6h. Memory +20% over baseline.

jake: do you have profiler traces? is this fragmentation or leaked refs?

maria: added an async heap dump and free-list dump. looks like the allocator's small-block pool (microblock size 64/128B) accumulates many tiny free segments but they aren't merged. free-list shows many adjacent free entries but they're split by metadata markers.

sophia: can you paste the free-list sample? curious about boundary tags.

maria: pasted below — it's a short sample from /var/run/kv/free-list.dump at T+5h

maria: ```
# free-list tail (slice)
[slice 0x7f8a3c000] size=64 free next=0x7f8a3c040 prev=0x0 tag=busy?0
[slice 0x7f8a3c040] size=128 free next=0x7f8a3c0c0 prev=0x7f8a3c000 tag=free
[slice 0x7f8a3c100] size=64 free next=0x7f8a3c140 prev=0x7f8a3c0c0 tag=free
[slice 0x7f8a3c140] size=64 used next=0x7f8a3c180 prev=0x7f8a3c100 tag=busy
# note: plenty of adjacent free ranges but we don't coalesce across the tag boundary
```

ben: that tag bit looks suspect — I remember a recent change where we made in-flight-eviction markers persistent until checkpoint to avoid races with KV hot-movements.

olga: right — we intentionally set a 'stale-reserve' flag on recently-evicted microblocks so hot re-inserts don't thrash. But we planned to clear it on compaction. Looks like the clear path didn't run under latency-favor kernel.

tim: I ran a quick bisect. The regression correlates with commit f3c2e9b (kernel selector: prefer fused kernels for short batches). When fused path is active, background compactor thread gets starved by long tail latencies and its tick misses.

jake: so two issues: (1) stale-reserve tags not cleared because compactor schedule missed, (2) compactor starved on fused kernel path. Both cause microblocks to remain split and not coalesced. Good catch.

sophia: any perf counters showing compactor ticks? the agent should log compactor-heartbeat.

maria: yes — attached snippet of /var/log/kv/compactor.log

maria: ```
[00:00:10] compactor: tick ok
[00:10:12] compactor: tick ok
# after kernel switch to fused
[02:15:01] compactor: missed tick (budget exceeded)
[02:16:01] compactor: missed tick (budget exceeded)
[02:17:01] compactor: missed tick (budget exceeded)
# compactor resumed after 30m
[02:47:01] compactor: tick ok (catchup)
```

ben: 30m of missed compaction is enough to accumulate thousands of 64B fragments. At 4k qps that's a lot.

olga: workaround we used in dev: make stale-reserve auto-clear after N seconds (e.g., 60s) even if compactor misses. Risk is a bit of reinsert churn but better than memory growth.

tim: agree. For a short-term patch: (A) Add time-decay auto-clear on stale-reserve flag. (B) Backoff fused-kernel aggressiveness when compactor backlog > threshold.

jake: performance-wise, autop-run and unit tests? wants a patch

sophia: also thinking of a compaction opportunistic merge: when allocator services a free request, look at neighbors and merge on-the-fly instead of waiting for compactor.

maria: allocator-on-alloc coalesce is doable at micro cost if we take the per-slab spinlock. But we need to measure lock contention — might increase tail latency.

ben: idea: perform coalesce only if request latency budget allows (we already track per-request budget). If within budget, do a single local coalesce step; otherwise enqueue to compactor.

maria: wrote a quick prototype: when popping free 64B slice, check next neighbor, if free and owned by same slab, try CAS merge for single step.

maria: microbenchmark results (local laptop sim):

maria: ```
baseline: 95th=12ms
alloc-coalesce-on-path: 95th=13ms (+8%)
alloc-coalesce-if-budget: 95th=12.3ms (+2.5%)
compactor-only: 95th=11.8ms (-1.5%)
```

olga: that's promising — conditional coalesce buys most of the benefit with low tail hit.

tim: for scheduling, we should also make compactor tick real-time safe: reduce compactor's dependence on worker CPU shares. Put it on a dedicated low-priority thread pinned to isolated core when available.

sophia: long-term: tune microblock sizes. We currently have fixed microblock bins [32,64,128,256]. For long-context workloads with many tiny keys, maybe add a 48B bin to reduce internal fragmentation.

ben: if we add 48B bin we need to re-eval packing heuristics and impact on cache footprint. Might reduce waste but increase allocator complexity.

jake: let's triage: 1) short-term patch (auto-clear + backoff fused-path), 2) mid-term (alloc coalesce-if-budget + compactor pinned thread), 3) long-term (bin size tuning + smart packer). I'll open a PR for (1).

maria: PR opened: https://git.internal/r/redwood/kv/compare/auto-clear-stale

maria: CI shows unit tests pass, integration flagged a flaky on high qps load in the fused path — looks like our test harness doesn't simulate compactor starvation.

tim: I'll add a chaotic-kernel test that runs fused path with background compactor disabled to reproduce. Add it to nightly perf.

olga: we should also add a metric: free-run-length histogram per-slab so ops team can alert when free-run-length spikes.

sophia: good idea. add alert: free-run-length P99 > 3k for 10m -> page an eng-runtime oncall.

ben: one more note — disk-backed cold page reclaim interacts with this: when compactor misses and we have many small free runs, page reclaim may swap out slabs causing further fragmentation. We'll include that in incident notes.

maria: TL;DR in checklist form:
- [x] identify regression commit
- [x] root cause: compactor starvation + stale-reserve flag
- [x] short-term PR auto-clear + fused backoff (PR open)
- [ ] mid-term: alloc coalesce-if-budget (prototype done)
- [ ] infra: pinned compactor thread + chaotic-kernel test
- [ ] long-term: microblock bin tuning + free-run histogram metric

jake: thanks team — let's land the short-term patch today and schedule a follow-up to implement coalesce-on-path next sprint. :thumbsup: 

ci-bot: build passed for auto-clear-stale (linux/amd64), integration pending. 

maria: assigning follow-ups in JIRA: KV-2483 (auto-clear), KV-2484 (coalesce-if-budget), KV-2485 (compactor-pin), KV-2486 (bin-tune)

olga: ping me for a review on the coalesce proto, I have some lock-free ideas.

sophia: adding diagnostics dashboard widget: free-run-length heatmap + compactor backlog.

tim: I'll own the chaotic-kernel test. ETA 2 days.

maria: thanks all — closing thread for now, will post updates in the PR and JIRA.
